title: Add weighted-seed perturbation resilience latch and CI sensitivity prober
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Introduce a configurable CI gate that runs weighted random-seed perturbations over prompt-sets to detect sensitivity regressions; ships with a resilience latch that quarantines changes with high instability until triage.
description:
Context & motivation: We see recurring intermittent regressions where small changes in tokenization, sampling defaults, or runtime kernels cause large variance for a subset of prompts. Existing cohort-level SLOs surface failures but provide little signal about sensitivity to RNG/seed changes. This PR introduces a lightweight, opt-in probe that runs controlled seed perturbations during CI and a 'resilience latch' that gates merges when seed-driven instability exceeds configured thresholds.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a Weighted Seed Perturbation Prober (runs n perturbations per prompt with configurable weight distribution), a Resilience Latch that integrates with the CI decision layer, new e2e and unit tests, CI workflow wiring, dashboards and a short how-to doc. The probe is intentionally conservative: default sample size=5, top-percentile breakdown, and an exponential weight schedule so long-tail prompts are exercised more frequently.

Design notes and configuration: The probe is implemented as eval_harness.probers.seed_perturbation.SeedPerturbationProber; it accepts a prompt set, perturbation budget, and weight map (jsonlines remote or inline in defaults.yaml). The latch lives in eval_harness.latches.resilience_latch.ResilienceLatch and exposes two signals: instability_score (0-1) and signal_reason (top offending prompt ids). Configuration keys added: eval.prober.seed_perturbation.enabled (default false), eval.prober.seed_perturbation.samples, eval.prober.seed_perturbation.weight_scheme, eval.latch.resilience.threshold. The CI hook is ci/hooks/weighted_seed_probe.yml and is gated behind a feature flag (eval.ci.enable_seed_probe) to avoid immediate rollout to all repos.

Failure modes and fallback policy: If the probe job itself times out or fails, the latch will mark the run as neutral (no block) and emit a telemetry event for investigation; only explicit instability_score >= threshold will block. For teams that opt-in, the latch will produce an explanation artifact with a ranked list of examples for triage.

How to run locally: 
- Activate virtualenv and install test deps
- From repo root: ./ci/scripts/run_prober.sh --prompts examples/perturbation_demo_prompts.jsonl --samples 7 --weight-scheme exp
Sample prober output (truncated) included as artifact on CI.

Security & perf: Probe runs are CPU-light but may increase CI runtime; added a budget guard to CI workflow and an optional warm cache checkpoint to reduce tokenization variance noise. No secrets or key rotations are involved.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of prober harness and latch
- [x] Unit tests for metric calculation and weight schedule
- [x] E2E smoke test that runs 3 perturbations against a small prompt set
- [x] CI workflow YAML and feature flag gating
- [x] Docs: docs/ci/seed-perturbation.md with configuration examples

Related work: builds on ENG-2147 (cohort sensitivity research) and references SUP-4123 incident notes for observed flakiness.

Notes on uniqueness: weighted seeds prioritize long-tail prompts (we observed a 3x higher failure rate in 10% of prompts during internal experiments) and the resilience latch differs from prior soft-fail sentinels by returning a structured explanation artifact to speed triage.
